features.name: Nothing published until both sign-offs are green
features.label: nothing published until both are green
features.promise: A publish cannot proceed until both the code review (screens 11 and 12) and the outcome sign-off (screen 13) have passed, and the publish carries both.
features.howToVerify: With a change whose code review is approved but whose outcome sign-off is not (and again with the reverse), open the publish step on screen 07 and confirm the destination choices cannot be committed; approve the second one and confirm the same publish then proceeds and shows both sign-offs attached.
features.notes: Flow map edge label 43:91 and the "Choose where it goes" caption 43:40 "Both sign-offs attached".
features.defect: The outcome half cannot be given at all, so the gate can never open, and the publishes that are reachable are not gated by it. verification.vue's 'Sign off on the outcome' (verified live on /barn/extensions/base/verification, sitting under '2 of 4 met, 2 still to look at') calls its own signOff(), which sets a local {by, on} and writes a `## Verification` block into BRIEF.md. It does not call signOutcome(), and no screen anywhere does - grep for signOutcome across pages and components returns nothing. So signoffs.outcome is never written, distributionGate can never reach 'open', and distributeExtension is unreachable in any case (see 00-cross-screen-oci-gate). Nothing blocks the two publishes the product can perform: 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' both read 'No sign-off' and neither calls the gate.
features.evidence: The rule is now expressed in code and the record behind it is real. gateFrom()/distributionGate() return awaiting-code when the code review is missing and awaiting-outcome when the outcome is, and assertGateOpen() refuses both, in the one function that distributes. Screen 07 reads the record and draws the two rows: the live publish dialog rendered 'SIGN-OFFS / Code review / Is it safe? / Not signed off yet.' and 'Outcome sign-off / Does it do the job? / Not signed off yet.' The code half is writable and durable - another verifier's Approve on screen 12 created ConfigMap barn-review-base holding {"signoffs":{"code":{"verdict":"approved","principal":"local://user-btc48","name":"Default Admin","at":"2026-08-23T06:08:21.876Z","sha":"5814a08","packet":0}}}, which I read straight out of the cluster.

features.name: The brief sits on the main path before the build
features.label: Agree the brief — The need, the open questions, the criteria · Screen 10
features.promise: Agreeing the brief is a required stage between describing what you want (screen 02) and building it (screen 03), unlike checking the diff yourself (screen 04), which is explicitly optional.
features.howToVerify: Create a new extension from screen 02 and confirm the route passes through the brief on screen 10 before the workspace on screen 03; confirm by contrast that screen 04 can be skipped.
features.notes: Flow map: green connectors 43:50 and 43:53 put 43:11 between 43:8 and 43:16 on the main path, while 43:21 marks screen 04 "Optional". Rationale row 44:41: "It is only cheap to catch before the code exists".
features.defect: The rule is about the build, and building without a brief is still free. brief.vue still renders a 'Skip the brief' ghost button (skip() at line 991, the button at line 1199) whose only action is `$router.push({ name: EDITOR_ROUTE })` with no BRIEF.md written, and /barn/editor/:extension is directly addressable - screen 01's row menu 'Open in the workspace' goes straight there. So the brief is exactly as skippable as screen 04, which the flow map marks optional, and what the packet refusal moves is the hand-over, not stage 3 -> 4.
features.evidence: The hand-over is now structurally gated on the brief, which is real: assemblePacket() throws 'This change has no brief. The brief is what a reviewer compares the change against and what the outcome sign-off walks, so a change cannot be handed over without one', and distributionGate() returns the 'no-brief' state with its own sentence. The create route also still passes through the brief - screen 02's only submit is 'Draft the brief', and agree() writes BRIEF.md then pushes EDITOR_ROUTE with ?brief=1, which editor.vue now reads (handBriefOver) and hands to the assistant as the session's first instruction.

features.name: No capability of the current build is lost
features.label: Keeps everything the current build does: CLI, files, GitHub import, publish, settings.
features.promise: The redesign is additive: the CLI, the files view, GitHub import, publish and settings all remain available, and the raw terminal output in particular is still reachable one click away and still the source of truth.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each of the five capabilities is still reachable in the running Studio, and that the raw assistant output is reachable in one click from the activity stream on screen 03.
features.notes: Cover point one (29:13); rationale row 27:16 "Raw output is still there, one click away, and still the source of truth".
features.defect: The GitHub publish lost a capability the current build had, and the dialogs in front of it now describe behaviour that is gone. (1) 'Push the source to GitHub' now runs handOverForReview() -> assemblePacket(), which throws 'This change has no brief...' for any extension without BRIEF.md. Reachable in practice, because brief.vue still offers 'Skip the brief'. Before this wave the same button pushed the source regardless. (2) assemblePacket() sweeps the whole working tree into a commit ('Uncommitted work, swept in at the hand-over', review.ts line 514-517) *before* it checks for the brief or for anything else, so a refused hand-over still moves HEAD; with no baseline ref anywhere in this cluster the baseline resolves to HEAD, and the Changes tab and screens 04 and 12 then show nothing at all for work that is still uncommitted-in-spirit. (3) PublishGithubModal ('This pushes straight to main... It does not open a pull request, and there is nothing here to undo it with') and PublishModal's GitHub row ('not a pull request: it pushes to the repository's default branch (main) directly') both still describe the removed behaviour, so the one dialog standing between a person and the push tells them the opposite of what it will do.
features.evidence: Four of the five capabilities are intact and two improved. CLI: the workspace's Terminal tab is still the pod's exec session (xterm rendered live) and the raw output is still one click from the stream - [data-testid="barn-open-raw-output"] under the last turn, and 'Open the terminal' in the empty state. Files: the Files tab lists the tree and the branch/commit history ('5814a08 Reviewed: 1 file', '8a704fb The seeded extension'), and screen 05 still renders. GitHub import: 'Import from GitHub' is still in the publish split menu and the import dialog is now a wizard. Settings: improved - a real page at /barn/settings plus a credential-only dialog, both through studio-settings.ts. Local publish: unchanged and deliberately ungated, with a comment in publishExtension() saying it must stay so. The new mandatory `branch` argument on publishExtensionToGithub() breaks no caller: its only two callers, handOverForReview() and distributeExtension(), both pass one, and no .vue calls it.

features.name: A requested change arrives as an assistant instruction
features.label: Goes straight back to the workspace with the comment already loaded into the assistant — the reviewer never writes the fix themselves
features.promise: A reviewer's comment, from either the code review or the outcome sign-off, is carried into the author's workspace already loaded into the assistant as the instruction to work from, and the reviewer is never asked to write the fix.
features.howToVerify: Comment on a hunk on screen 12 and use "Send to the assistant", then open the author's workspace on screen 03 and confirm the reviewer's exact wording is present as a pending assistant instruction that the author must still approve.
features.notes: Flow map "Changes requested" (43:44/43:46) is fed by amber arrows from both "Code review" (43:82) and "Outcome sign-off" (43:85); rationale row 44:32 adds "the author still approves it".
features.defect: There is no comment, so the ?comment=<id> receiver is a producer-less handoff. addComment() and markCommentSent() exist in review.ts and no screen calls addComment - grep across pages and components returns nothing - so no comment record is ever created and no link carrying one is ever produced. A live text scan of /barn/review/base/working found no 'comment' and no 'send to the assistant' control, and there is no per-hunk comment affordance, which is what the caption describes. Two smaller gaps: the reviewer's sentence goes straight into the pod's pane rather than arriving staged for the author, so 'the author still approves it' is not kept; and the workspace's activity stream records nothing for a request that came in this way, because recordTurn is only on the ?comment= path.
features.evidence: The route back is now real from both reviewers, and the transport is proven live. Screen 12's 'Request changes' requires a note, calls signCodeReview(verdict 'changes-requested', sha, note) so the refusal is on record with the signer, then askAssistant() with 'A reviewer looked at the working tree of the <ext> extension and asked for a change: <note>...', clears the deferral and routes to EDITOR_ROUTE with ?tab=terminal. That the words really arrive is visible in the pod: /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl holds a prompt record whose text is 'A reviewer looked at the working tree of the base extension and asked for a change: w1-review-lists audit probe 8817...', so a previous verifier's press landed in the pod's conversation. Screen 13 has the same shape per criterion (sendBack -> askAssistant with the criterion and the reviewer's note). editor.vue's receiving end is built too: it reads ?comment=<id>, loads the record with readComment(), records a turn, sends it with originStamp('review-comment'), and calls markCommentSent() only when delivery succeeded.

features.name: One diff against the last published version
features.label: collapsed into one diff against the last published version
features.promise: The reviewer is shown a single diff of the change against the last published version, not the sequence of intermediate edits that produced it.
features.howToVerify: Make an edit and then undo or supersede it before pushing, then open the change on screen 12 and confirm the diff shows only the net difference from the last published version and no intermediate state.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.defect: No extension in this cluster has a baseline, so no screen is actually measuring from a published version yet. base has no refs/barn/* at all; nodehealth is genuinely published (UIPlugin v0.1.0, endpoint on its own pod proxy) and still has no refs/barn/published/local, because it was published before this code shipped and nothing backfills. Live consequence on screen 12: /barn/review/base/working renders 'BRIEF.md +0 -16' measured against 5814a08 'Reviewed: 1 file' - a commit another reviewer made, not a published version. Second gap: baselineRef() is consumed only by components/BuildFailure.vue, so screens 04 and 12 use the baseline for the diff but never say which point they measured from, which is the sentence the design step asked for.
features.evidence: The mechanism landed and is correct. extensions.ts now defines BASELINE_OCI_REF (refs/barn/published/oci) and BASELINE_LOCAL_REF (refs/barn/published/local) and a BASELINE_SH that resolves oci, then local, then HEAD; workingDiff(), fileDiff(), changedFiles() and countChanges() all route through it, publishExtension() calls recordBaseline() after upsertUiPlugin() succeeds, and distributeExtension() moves the oci ref after a push lands. baselineRef() returns the sentence a screen should say ('measured against the last version that was handed over' / '...published into this Rancher' / 'nothing has been published yet, so this is measured against the last commit'). I proved the resolution order in an isolated git repository: with refs/barn/published/local set two commits back, the diff collapsed the intermediate commit and the working tree into one patch against the published point; with the ref removed, the same command measured from HEAD.

features.name: Connection state and permission mode are one state shown in two places
features.label: Connection state is a persistent strip in the panel: a dot, the account, and the permission mode as a real control.
features.promise: The account, connection state and assistant permission mode shown on the workspace strip (screen 03) and on the settings page (screen 09) are the same state, and settings is the one place all of it lives.
features.howToVerify: Change the permission mode on screen 09 and confirm the workspace strip on screen 03 reflects it without a reload, and vice versa; confirm no other modal edits the GitHub token.
features.notes: Rationale rows 27:25 ("Screens 03, 09") and 27:34; caption 23:918 "connection, permissions, access and data in one place", replacing the bare token modal (23:919).
features.defect: The permission mode is not a control in either place, so nothing can be changed in one and be true in the other. The settings card carries a warning banner reading 'Not settable, and not per user... Only the pod's start-up decides', and the workspace chip is a plain SPAN reading 'Edits apply without asking'. They are also not the same reading: settings computes the level from the pod's start-up command, while the chip is a hardcoded string in AssistantPanel.vue. The connection halves differ too - the strip reports the claude session in the pod, the settings page reports the GitHub credential - so the rule's 'same state in two places' holds for neither concern.
features.evidence: Screen 09 now exists and is the single home. /barn/settings renders 'Studio settings - Applies to everyone who uses Studio on this Rancher', with sign-off policy, 'What the assistant may do without asking' (the design's three levels, one marked 'In force' from detectPermission(), which reads the pod's own claude-session.sh out of the extension's ConfigMap), preview target, access and what is sent to the model. EditorSettingsModal.vue has been cut down to a credential prompt with a link to that page, and both it and the page write through studio-settings.ts, so exactly one code path stores the GitHub token. The strip on screen 03 is honest too: it reads assistantLogin() and rendered 'The assistant is not signed in - run /login in the terminal'.

features.name: Verification walks the criteria written in the brief
features.label: Acceptance criteria written in the brief become a checklist walked against the running build, with captured evidence and a second, separate sign-off.
features.promise: The acceptance criteria are authored once on screen 10 and are the same items walked, against the running build and with evidence captured, on screen 13.
features.howToVerify: Write a distinctive acceptance criterion in the brief on screen 10, take the change through to verification, and confirm screen 13 lists that exact criterion as a checklist item, exercised against the running build, with the captured evidence attached.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59 ("Screens 07 and 13"); caption 45:1206 "the criteria walked against the running build"; flow map 43:37.
features.evidence: Authored once on screen 10 and read as the same objects on screen 13. brief.vue's briefMarkdown() writes the heading `## How we will know it worked` followed by one `- [ ] <criterion>` per filled criterion; verification.vue's criteriaLines() reads sectionOf(brief, 'How we will know it worked') and takes every `- [ ]`/`- [x]` line, keyed on the criterion's own text. Verified live against real data: `kubectl -n barn exec deploy/barn-base-extension -- cat /app/pkg/base/BRIEF.md` holds four criteria, two ticked, and /barn/extensions/base/verification rendered exactly those four in the same order with the tally "2/4" and the two ticked ones already answered Yes. Walked against the running build: each row carries "Show me", which navigates the PreviewPanel (the extension's own dev server, framed on the right and reading "Loaded . just now") to the route the verdict was taken at, and the route is written back next to the verdict. Evidence is captured into the same file - the pod's BRIEF.md already contains the `## Verification` block with "- **Met**: ..." lines. I did not author a fresh criterion because BRIEF.md on the shared base pod is another verifier's working file; the write side and the read side use the identical heading and line syntax, and the round trip is observable on the existing four.

features.name: Built from components the dashboard already has
features.label: Everything below is achievable with components that already exist in the Rancher dashboard — SortableTable, LabeledInput, Banner, Card, Tabbed, AsyncButton — so none of this asks the team to invent new UI primitives.
features.promise: Every screen is realisable with existing Rancher dashboard primitives, and the Studio home list in particular uses the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page rather than a bespoke table.
features.howToVerify: Inspect the rendered markup of the Studio screens and confirm tables, inputs, banners, cards, tabs and async buttons are the dashboard's own components rather than reimplementations, and that screen 01 reads like the Clusters page table.
features.notes: Header note 27:5 of the rationale frame; rationale row 27:88 names the Clusters page pattern for screen 01.
features.defect: The rule's claim is true - nothing in the design needs a primitive the dashboard lacks - but the build does not honour it. The Studio reimplements Banner, Card, Tabbed, Button, Modal, Badge and Menu privately, and screen 01 is not the Clusters page's SortableTable.
features.evidence: Unchanged this wave, and the new surfaces follow the same pattern. The ten Studio pages are still built on the bespoke S-prefixed set in pkg/barn/components/ui (SBadge, SBanner, SButton, SCard, SChip, SEmpty, SField, SIcon, SLabel, SMenu, SModal, SPanel, SRow, STabs, SToolbar); the new pages/settings.vue imports SButton, SBanner, SCard, SChip, SIcon and SField from that set, and the new ImportStep.vue is a fresh wizard-chrome component whose own header says it is 'one screen's wizard chrome, not a primitive'. Screen 01 is still a hand-rolled grid: extensions.vue renders div.studio-home__table with div.studio-home__row children and its own COLUMNS array, not SortableTable. grep for "from '@shell" across pages returns nothing.

features.name: A guaranteed way back from any build failure
features.label: When it breaks — plain-language cause, one-click fix, guaranteed way back
features.promise: Every build is snapshotted so that a failure always has a state to roll back to, which means the snapshot has to be taken in the workspace before the change that breaks it.
features.howToVerify: Cause a build to fail from a known-good state and confirm screen 08 offers a snapshot of that state to roll back to, and that rolling back returns the workspace to it.
features.notes: Caption 23:915 and rationale row 27:97 "a snapshot to roll back to"; the snapshot is created on screen 03 and consumed on screen 08.
features.defect: The guarantee is still not met and the screen says so itself: 'nothing takes a snapshot automatically when a build succeeds yet, so this is the nearest point that exists rather than a guaranteed last working build.' Two reasons it lands there. recordWorkingBuild() only fires after a *successful publish*, not before the change that breaks the build, and it keeps its pointer in sessionStorage, so another tab or another person gets none of it. And the durable fallback, the baseline ref, does not exist for any extension in this cluster yet. The v-else copy quoted above is also now stale - publish-failure.ts does snapshot a successful publish - so the sentence understates what shipped while the guarantee still does not hold.
features.evidence: Screen 08 now offers a way back, which reverses the wave-1 finding that it offered none. Seeded sessionStorage['barn.publish.failure'] in my own page and opened /barn/extensions/base/build-failed: the panel rendered 'Roll back to the snapshot "before applying the suggested fix"' ([data-testid="barn-rollback"], enabled) beside 'Undo the last change', with the target described as 'Taken 2 minutes ago. A snapshot is a point somebody chose, not necessarily a build that worked. 3 changed files since.' findWayBack() in BuildFailure.vue resolves four candidates in order - the snapshot publish-failure.ts recordWorkingBuild() takes when a publish succeeds, then the baseline ref, then the newest hand snapshot, then the last commit - and names which one it landed on, so a target always exists. I did not press it: restoring base's tree would pull the ground out from under the other verifiers on this pod.

features.name: Iteration before the gate asks nobody
features.label: Iteration is completely ungated: dev preview and developer load ask nobody.
features.promise: Creating, building, previewing, breaking, rebuilding and developer-loading an extension never require anyone's approval, so no review or sign-off control may block any of them.
features.howToVerify: Make several edits in the workspace (screen 03), let a build fail and recover it (screen 08), and developer-load the result, confirming that no approval dialog, pending-review banner or disabled control appears at any point before screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 65:1083; flow map caption 43:18 "Readable activity, live preview, and no gates at all" and 43:24 "Everything before it is yours alone".
features.evidence: Drove 01 (/barn/extensions), 02 (/barn/extensions/new), 10 (brief), 03 (/barn/editor/base), 04 (review), 05 (files) and 08 (build-failed, with a seeded sessionStorage failure) in one session. No approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no control disabled for a review reason appeared anywhere. A text scan of the workspace for approval / sign off / signed off / gate / OCI / registry / blocked returned []. The Publish button was enabled on screen 03 while the extension had unreviewed working-tree changes, and screen 02's "Draft the brief" submit was enabled. Two extensions created by other verifiers during this run (demo, v02-new-extension) went straight to Building with no approval step. I did not create one myself, per the shared-pod rule.

features.name: The OCI publish gate
features.label: Push to an OCI repository — The one hard gate. Everything before it is yours alone · Screen 07
features.promise: There is exactly one hard gate in the whole product and it is the push to an OCI repository, the point at which the extension first becomes installable by other people.
features.howToVerify: From a freshly created extension, walk stages 01, 02, 10, 03 and 04 without ever being asked for an approval, then start a publish to an OCI repository on screen 07 and confirm that this is the first and only step that will not complete on the author's say-so alone.
features.notes: Flow map 43:22/43:24 and the guardrail note 43:93; rationale row 65:1083 states it as "The gate is the push to an OCI repository, where the extension first becomes installable by other people".
features.defect: Nothing in the running product can reach the gate, so the one hard gate is never crossed and never tried. PublishModal's TARGETS mark 'oci' and 'catalog' available: false, and confirm() emits only `TARGETS.filter(t => t.available && isChosen(t.id))`, so the OCI box has no checkbox at all (verified live: the OCI row rendered with no input and the reason 'Not built. Nothing in this Studio produces an OCI artefact or pushes one...'). The masthead's split menu offers only 'Publish to GitHub', 'Import from GitHub' and 'Remove local install'. editor.vue's onPublishChosen looks for ids 'oci' | 'repository' | 'distribute' - ids no component emits - so distributeExtension(), distributionGate() and distributionDestinations() are unreachable from every screen. Separately, /barn/settings draws a sign-off policy matrix whose 'Push to a repository' row is labelled 'The gate' and defaults to 'Code review: Required', and the page itself says 'Studio records this policy; it does not enforce it yet. Nothing in the publish path reads these values, so no publish is blocked by them today.'
features.evidence: Half of it is now real and I could establish exactly what it refuses. review.ts distributeExtension() opens with `const gate = await assertGateOpen(extension);` (line 912), and assertGateOpen throws a GateError carrying distributionGate()'s state whenever it is not 'open'. distributionGate() reads the review ConfigMap plus one exec into the pod and returns, in order: no-brief, no-packet, stale-packet (the tip has moved past the packet), changes-requested, awaiting-code, awaiting-outcome, same-signer, open - each with a whole sentence naming who it waits for. It is the only choke point: the other two ways out of the pod are publishExtension() (local, carrying a comment saying it must stay ungated forever) and publishExtensionToGithub(), which now refuses without a branch and has exactly two callers, both inside review.ts. Checked the live state: base has BRIEF.md, no refs/barn/packets/*, and no barn-review-base ConfigMap, so distributionGate('base') resolves to no-packet and assertGateOpen would throw. The ungated half also holds: walked 01, 02, 10, 03, 04, 05, 08, 11, 12 and 13 and was never asked for an approval; the publish dialog marks 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' as 'No sign-off' and states 'only the OCI push asks for them'.

features.name: The hand-off to review is a PR, and the PR is the record
features.label: hand-off · the PR is the record
features.promise: Crossing the gate hands the work from the author's lane to the reviewers' lane by producing a PR, and that PR is the durable record of the hand-off.
features.howToVerify: Push a change to an OCI repository and confirm the resulting queue entry on screen 11 is backed by a PR, and that the PR is reachable from the review surface as the record of the change.
features.notes: Flow map connector label 43:90 on the green connector running from "Push to an OCI repository" (43:22) into "Code review" (43:28).
features.defect: The record is written and never read, the chip cannot find what the hand-over makes, and both dialogs describe the behaviour that was removed. (1) No screen reads record.packets, so packets[n].pr is invisible. (2) Screen 12's chip calls findOpenPullRequest(extension, repo, this.branch) where branch is the pod's *current* branch, but a packet's branch is created with `git branch -f` and never checked out, so the head it searches for is never the packet's - the chip cannot find the PR the hand-off produced. (3) PublishGithubModal still renders 'This pushes straight to main in that repository. It does not open a pull request, and there is nothing here to undo it with', and PublishModal's GitHub row (read live) still says 'Not reversible from here, and not a pull request: it pushes to the repository's default branch (main) directly.' Both are now false. (4) Unverifiable end to end here: no GitHub token and no repository are configured on this Studio, so no PR could actually be created.
features.evidence: The product can now create the PR. extensions.ts gained createPullRequest() (POST /repos/<repo>/pulls, returning an existing open PR for the same head rather than failing on a re-push) and commentOnPullRequest(); handOverForReview() assembles the packet, pushes branch barn/<extension>/<n> instead of HEAD:refs/heads/main, opens the PR with a body naming the packet, the baseline it is collapsed against and the whole brief, and writes {ref, branch, sha, base, pr, prError, pushError} into the review record. publishExtensionToGithub() now refuses a push with no branch, so nothing can go to main by accident.

features.name: Preview and published are separated by an explicit line
features.label: The same live preview, plus an explicit boundary: preview is yours alone, snapshotted per build, and publishing is a separate deliberate act.
features.promise: Work in the live preview affects only the author and is snapshotted per build; nothing reaches anyone else until the separate, deliberate publish on screen 07.
features.howToVerify: Make a visible change in the workspace preview on screen 03, then confirm from another session or another user that the installed extension is unchanged until a publish is performed on screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 27:52 ("Screens 03, 07"); the cover's reading note 29:41 calls it "an explicit line between preview and published".
features.defect: 'Yours alone' is still false and is a structural gap, not an oversight: there is one pod per extension at one cluster URL, every Studio user sees the same preview, and other verifiers' edits to base appeared in my session while I worked. REVIEW-SYSTEM.md names this explicitly as something it will not fix. 'Snapshotted per build' is also only true of a successful publish, not of a build, and the pointer lives in sessionStorage.
features.evidence: The separation itself holds and is enforced. The preview is the pod's dev server behind the apiserver service proxy (the iframe src on /barn/editor/base is /k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/barn/services/http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/); publishing is a separate deliberate act through PublishModal, whose footer read 'Nothing is ticked, so nothing will be published.' base's working tree has been edited all day and nothing has been installed from it. Screen 11 says the same in words: 'Nothing in this list is live. Everything here is still running only in its author's preview.' The 'snapshotted per build' qualifier is now partly kept - publish-failure.ts recordWorkingBuild() snapshots the tree of every publish that succeeds.

features.name: Prompt provenance and the brief survive from authoring into review
features.label: Every hunk carries the prompt that produced it, and the whole change carries its brief.
features.promise: The prompt that caused each hunk is captured during authoring on screen 03 and is still attached, per hunk, when the change is reviewed on screen 12, and the brief from screen 10 travels with the change as a whole.
features.howToVerify: Author a change with two distinguishable prompts in the workspace, push it, then on screen 12 confirm each hunk shows the prompt that produced it and that the change header shows the brief written on screen 10.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:5; caption 45:1204 "prompt provenance per hunk".
features.defect: Screen 12 cannot show provenance even when it exists. provenanceFor() is called from exactly one place, assemblePacket(), which serialises it into a git note on the packet; review-change.vue does not import it and renders no per-hunk prompt column - a live text scan of /barn/review/base/working for 'prompt' and 'no prompt recorded' returned false for both. The brief half still survives correctly: screen 12's left column is headed 'The packet' and renders the base brief's problem, who has it, what changes, non-goals and its four criteria, all read from BRIEF.md. Two things have to land for the prompt half: a signed-in claude in the pod so turns end in Barn-Turn: commits, and a consumer of provenanceFor() on screen 12.
features.evidence: The capture is wired and firing; nothing is recorded because the pod's claude is signed out; and the review side has nowhere to show it. Capture: /seed/barn-provenance.mjs is present in the live base pod and /app/.home/.claude/settings.json registers UserPromptSubmit -> 'node /seed/barn-provenance.mjs prompt', PostToolUse (Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit) -> 'touch', and Stop -> 'stop' beside the existing credentials hook. It works and it attributes: I sent two prompts from the workspace composer and /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl gained {"kind":"prompt","turn":"tmt5fbhv6rostd","prompt":"w2xc probe one 57496","screen":"workspace","principal":"local://user-btc48","who":"Default Admin","head":"94f0478..."} and the same for probe two, while prompts other screens sent without an origin stamp recorded screen '' and principal '' - exactly the honesty rule the design states. Nothing completes: the pod has no /app/.home/.claude/.credentials.json and the workspace status row reads 'The assistant is not signed in - run /login in the terminal', so the Stop hook never runs, every turn has endedAt '' and commit '', and no commit in the repository carries a Barn-Turn: trailer. `node /seed/barn-provenance.mjs report` in the pod therefore answers {"available":true,"base":"8a704fb...","files":[{"path":"BRIEF.md","hunks":[{"from":1,"to":34,"added":34,"turns":[],"unrecorded":34}]}]} - every line 'changed in the pod, no prompt recorded', which is the correct answer and not a useful one.

features.name: Live is reversible from the extension list
features.label: Reversible from the extension list
features.promise: Publishing is not a one-way door: a live extension can be taken back from the Studio home list on screen 01.
features.howToVerify: Publish an extension, return to /dashboard/barn/extensions, and confirm the row for the live extension offers a way to reverse the publish.
features.notes: Flow map terminal state "Live" (43:41) and its caption 43:43; the reversal control lives on screen 01, not on screen 07.
features.evidence: Screen 01's per-row menu carries "Remove the local install", and it is live rather than aspirational. Opened all three row menus on /barn/extensions: nodehealth, which is published ("Running on: catalog . v0.1.0"), showed "Remove the local install v0.1.0" enabled; base and demo, which are not installed, showed it disabled with the reason "not installed". removeLocalInstall() resolves the plugin through packageIdentity() and DELETEs the UIPlugin in the cattle-ui-plugin namespace, which is the whole of what a local publish creates (upsertUiPlugin), leaving the pod and its tree untouched. Confirmed by reading rather than clicking - removing another verifier's install is destructive shared state. The GitHub push is not reversible from screen 01, but that is a push to someone else's repository rather than the "Live" state the map marks reversible.

features.name: Every recovery route returns to the same workspace
features.label: amber is recovery — and every recovery route leads back into the same workspace rather than out of the product
features.promise: Both failure routes drawn on the map, a broken build and a rejected review, end back in the author's workspace rather than in a separate remediation surface or outside the product.
features.howToVerify: Trigger a build failure and apply its fix, confirming the user lands back in the same workspace; separately, request changes as a reviewer and confirm the author is returned to that same workspace rather than to a new screen.
features.notes: Flow map legend 43:4; the amber arrows 43:62/43:65 leave and re-enter the same "Build it and watch it" box (43:16), and "Changes requested" (43:44) routes back to it.
features.evidence: Both amber routes land back in the same workspace route. Screen 08: fixIt() and retry() both `$router.push({ name: EDITOR_ROUTE, params: { extension } })` (retry adds `query: { publish: 'local' }`); seeChanges() goes to screen 04, which itself carries a "Back to assistant" button (observed in its button list). Verified live by loading /barn/extensions/base/build-failed with a seeded sessionStorage failure: the "Ways back" block rendered exactly "Fix it with the assistant", "See what changed", "Try the publish again". Screen 12: requestChanges() pushes EDITOR_ROUTE for the same extension. No recovery route leaves the product or opens a separate remediation surface.

features.name: The review packet accumulates in the background and is assembled at the push
features.label: the review packet accumulates quietly in the background. It is only assembled and handed to a reviewer at the push to a repository
features.promise: Everything a reviewer will need is captured continuously while the author works, but it is only assembled into a review packet and handed over at the moment of the push.
features.howToVerify: Work in the workspace for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue (screen 11), then push once and confirm a complete packet, including material captured across all of those earlier cycles, appears in a single queue entry.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.defect: Nothing accumulates and the queue still ignores packets entirely. review-queue.vue load() calls listExtensions() and then enrich() per row with countChanges/changedFiles/readExtensionFile - a dirty working tree is still what puts you in somebody's queue. No screen reads record.packets: grep for '.packets' across pages and components returns nothing. Live proof of the contradiction: base has no refs/barn/packets/* in its pod and no review ConfigMap, nothing has ever been handed over, and /barn/review still shows 'Waiting on you 1' with a base row reading '3 files - +2 -16 - 4 acceptance criteria - WAITING 16 minutes - BRANCH main - Unsaved'. The only thing accumulating in the background is /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl, and it currently holds prompts with no completed turns.
features.evidence: The 'assembled at the push' half is now built and is only reachable from the push. assemblePacket() sweeps anything uncommitted into a commit, refuses without a git history and without BRIEF.md, allocates n = max(existing packets) + 1, writes refs/barn/packets/<n> at the tip, attaches the blame-resolved provenance index as a git note on refs/notes/barn-provenance, and creates branch barn/<extension>/<n>. Its only caller is handOverForReview(), which is the GitHub push. Nothing else calls it.

features.name: The build is compared back to its own brief at sign-off
features.label: The build is compared back to its own brief, and anything outside it is flagged during sign-off — accept it into the brief, or take it out.
features.promise: At outcome sign-off the built change is diffed against the brief that started it, and anything not in the brief is surfaced with two resolutions: accept it into the brief, or remove it.
features.howToVerify: Have the assistant make a change beyond what the brief asked for, take it to screen 13, and confirm the extra work is flagged as outside the brief and offers both accepting it into the brief and taking it out.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:68; requires the screen 10 brief to still be attached to the change at screen 13.
features.defect: There are still no resolutions. The drifted branch renders a warning banner plus a static list of term -> files (verification.vue lines 1276-1288) and nothing to press; there is no 'accept it into the brief' and no 'take it out' anywhere in the file. The flag is a note, not a decision point.
features.evidence: Unchanged this wave. The Scope card on /barn/extensions/base/verification is real and did the comparison live: it read '3 files changed / Nothing this change adds mentions monitoring alerting history beyond belong hours - the words the brief used to say what it was not doing.' verification.vue extracts the non-goal terms from `## What we are deliberately not doing`, applies a stop-list, scans only the added lines of the working diff and skips BRIEF.md, and has four states (unstated, nothing-changed, clear, drifted).

features.name: Re-review is incremental across visits
features.label: A "since your last look" filter, and a banner on the queue row saying how many changes landed since you approved.
features.promise: Per-reviewer state persists between visits, so a reviewer returning after the author has pushed again sees how many changes landed since they approved and can filter the diff to just those.
features.howToVerify: Approve a change as a reviewer, push further changes as the author, then return to screen 11 and confirm the queue row banners the number of changes since that approval, and that screen 12 offers a "since your last look" filter restricted to them.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:23, "Screens 11 and 12".
features.defect: No 'since your last look' filter exists on screen 12 at all - grep for 'since' in review-change.vue returns nothing and a live text scan of /barn/review/base/working for 'since your last look' returned false. On screen 11 the packet-based banner can never fire because no reviewer's look is ever recorded and no packet is ever created. Wiring markLook() into review-change.vue's load is the missing line.
features.evidence: The per-reviewer machinery was built this wave and is dead. review.ts defines Look, markLook(), lastLook(), deferPacket(), clearOwnDeferral(), migrateDeferral() and sinceLastLook(), keyed by a hash of the Rancher principal, and review-queue.vue calls sinceLastLook(name) per row and prefers its banner. But nothing calls markLook() - grep across pages and components returns nothing - so looks stays empty, lastPacket is always 0, behind is always false and banner is always ''. The live record confirmed it: after a code sign-off was written, barn-review-base held "looks": {}. The queue falls back to changesSince(gate.code, history, changes), which counts commits after the code sign-off's sha; that is per sign-off rather than per reviewer, and it needs an approval to exist first.

features.name: Two sign-offs by two different people
features.label: Splits "is it safe?" from "does it work?" — two questions, two people, neither able to answer the other's.
features.promise: The code review is signed by a developer and the outcome sign-off by the person who asked for the change; they are separate acts by separate roles, not one approval recorded twice.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the code review record (screen 12) and the verification record (screen 13) carry distinct signer identities and distinct timestamps, and that signing one does not mark the other complete.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59; flow map 43:32 "A developer" and 43:37 "The person who asked"; cover point three 29:21 "a separate outcome sign-off by the person who asked".
features.defect: The rule can never be exercised, and the second role is never established. (1) No screen writes an outcome sign-off (see 00-cross-screen-both-signoffs-required), so two principals can never both be on record and the same-signer branch is dead. (2) signOutcome() refuses a signer who is not the principal in the brief's `## Who asked` section, but nothing writes that section - grep for 'Who asked' across pages and components returns nothing, and the live review queue row for base says so in its own words: 'nothing records who asked for this'. So even if it were called, it would accept whoever is standing there. (3) Screen 13's record still carries no signer at all: it writes lines like '- **Met**: ...' into BRIEF.md. (4) Nothing checks that the code reviewer is a developer, and REVIEW-SYSTEM.md is explicit that it will not.
features.evidence: The comparison is enforced rather than merely recorded, in the one place a distribution goes through: distributionGate() returns the 'same-signer' state when code.principal === outcome.principal, with the sentence 'Both sign-offs on packet N carry the same person... one person answering both is one opinion recorded twice', and assertGateOpen() throws on it. Identity is now real too - currentSigner() reads the apiserver's SelfSubjectReview plus /v3/users?me=true and throws rather than recording an unattributable decision, and the live barn-review-base record I read carried principal local://user-btc48 and name 'Default Admin' on the code sign-off.

features.promise: Under each extension name a second line explains what the extension is or what its state means right now.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each row's name cell renders a second, muted line and that its text tracks the row's state (building, failed, published, draft).
features.notes: Drawn subtitles: 8:158 description, 8:179 changes waiting, 8:200 compiling, 8:221 released version, 8:242 build error location, 8:263 template it started from. The copy differs per state, so it is not a static description field.
features.evidence: Every name cell renders a second muted line and each one matched the row's real state: base "1 change waiting for your review" (git status in the pod: 1 entry), nodehealth "2 changes waiting for your review" (git status: 2 entries), demo "Compiling - the preview reloads when it finishes" (deployment scaled 0/0), q11probe "On main, nothing uncommitted" (an extension another agent created mid-run, ready with a clean tree). A published-but-clean row would read "Released as v<x> to this Rancher".

features.name: Running on cell
features.label: e.g. 'local, prod-eu', 'local (preview)', 'catalog - 12 clusters', '-'
features.promise: The Running on column names where the extension is currently loaded, distinguishing preview-only from published-to-catalog, with an em dash when it runs nowhere.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each row's target text matches the extension's actual install target, and that an unpublished draft shows the dash placeholder.
features.evidence: Three distinct values, all cross-checked. nodehealth reads "catalog · v0.1.0" and `kubectl get uiplugins -A` shows nodehealth 0.1.0 installed in cattle-ui-plugin-system. base and q11probe read "local (preview)": their deployments are 1/1 and neither has a UIPlugin. demo reads "-": its deployment is 0/0 and it has no UIPlugin. So published-to-catalog, preview-only and nowhere are each distinguished from live readings.

features.name: Last change cell
features.label: e.g. '4 min ago', 'just now', '1 week ago'
features.promise: The Last change column shows a relative time since the extension last changed.
features.howToVerify: Change an extension and confirm its Last change cell updates to 'just now' and then ages.
features.evidence: extensionDetail's lastTouched is live. Before: base '4 min ago' (title 'An uncommitted file was edited then. The last commit is older.' - its last commit is 2026-08-21T22:37, over a day old, so the cell is reading the working tree not the log), nodehealth '6 hours ago', demo '-'. I then ran `touch /app/pkg/nodehealth/BRIEF.md` in the nodehealth pod and reloaded: nodehealth's cell became 'just now'. The sort moved with it - with 'Last change' sorted descending nodehealth went from second place (behind base '7 min ago') to first. The header itself sorts and reverses: descending gave base, nodehealth, demo, v02w1 and a second click gave demo, v02w1, nodehealth, base, with aria-sort flipping descending/ascending.

features.name: Sort by Last change
features.label: Last change
features.promise: The 'Last change' column header carries a sort glyph, so clicking it sorts by recency.
features.howToVerify: Click the 'Last change' header and confirm rows reorder by timestamp, newest first then oldest first.
features.notes: Sort affordance drawn as node 56:1096. The cells hold relative times ('4 min ago', '1 week ago'), so sorting has to use the underlying timestamp.
features.evidence: Sorts on the timestamp, not the rendered string, and I proved it rather than assumed it. With the real data the two orderings coincide, so I shifted only Date.now() forward 24h in the page (Date.parse of the ISO timestamps is untouched) so that the older extension renders the LATER-sorting string: base (older) rendered "2 days ago" and nodehealth (newer) rendered "1 day ago". First click gave aria-sort=descending and the order nodehealth "1 day ago", base "2 days ago", demo "-" - i.e. newest first. A string sort would have put "2 days ago" on top. Second click gave ascending and the exact reverse (demo "-", base, nodehealth). The header carries a chevron that turns from chevronDown to chevronUp and gets the --on treatment.

features.name: Extension state badge
features.label: Live / Unsaved / Building / Published / Failed / Draft
features.promise: Each row leads with a Rancher-style state pill naming the extension's current state.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each row renders a state pill and that the six states in the component set (Live, Unsaved, Building, Published, Failed, Draft) each render with the right colour.
features.notes: Component set 3:42 'State Badge', described as mirroring the Rancher cluster-state pill. Instances: 8:153 Live, 8:174 Unsaved, 8:195 Building, 8:216 Published, 8:237 Failed, 8:258 Draft.
features.evidence: Every row leads with an .s-badge pill and each one is a live reading, cross-checked. base and nodehealth: "Unsaved" (s-badge--warning, #c9a227 on #fdf6e3) - git status in each pod shows 1 and 2 uncommitted entries. demo: "Building" (s-badge--info, #3d98d3 on #deebf7) - `kubectl -n barn get deploy` shows barn-demo-extension 0/0. q11probe, an extension another agent created 55 seconds earlier: "Live" (s-badge--success, #3e8c4f on #ebf4ec) - deployment 1/1, clean tree, and no UIPlugin, so not Published. nodehealth is the one row with a UIPlugin (v0.1.0) and it correctly badges Unsaved rather than Published because uncommitted work outranks publication. All six tone tokens resolve to distinct real colours on the page. Two caveats, neither a hardcoded value: I could not observe Published or Failed with real data during the run, and stateOf() can only ever return building/unsaved/published/live - 'failed' and 'draft' are unreachable from this screen except as the pre-enrichment default.

Screen 10 still says so in as many words: base's brief screen carries 'A request often names a solution rather than the problem behind it, and this Studio cannot tell you which this one is: nothing here has read it.' The challenge is delegated, not performed - extension-placement.ts:353 appends an instruction to the generated CLAUDE.md asking the pod's assistant to say so - and I did not observe that instruction firing.

Read the wiring instead and drove everything up to the press. The masthead's Publish opens PublishModal (editor.vue @publish="choosingPublish = true"); the modal rendered the real change ('2 files - +19 -8'), a settable version, four destinations of which 'Load into this Rancher' is tickable and marked 'No sign-off', and a footer reading 'Nothing is ticked, so nothing will be published.' Circumstantial evidence that the path works: the nodehealth extension has a live UIPlugin at v0.1.0 whose endpoint is exactly that pod-proxy URL shape.

features.evidence: base's card was topped with a tinted banner ([data-testid=queue-since], undo icon) reading '1 uncommitted file since Default Admin approved this on 2026-08-22.' It is counted, not claimed: the sign-off named commit 8a704fb, changesSince located that sha in the pod's git log and counted the commits above it (none) plus the uncommitted files (one, BRIEF.md), and the name and date came out of the record I wrote. No other row carried a banner, and the banner disappeared when the record was flipped to changes-requested. One thing the next person should know: the packet-based sentence from review.ts's sinceLastLook() can never fire today. It needs a Look with packet > 0, and the only writers of a Look are markLook() and deferPacket(), neither of which is called from any page (grep -rn 'markLook|deferPacket' over pkg/barn hits only review.ts's own definitions). So row.since always falls through to the code-sign-off count, which is the half that works.
